 The Critics Choice Association’s 9th Annual Celebration of Black Cinema & Television took place at the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles on Monday, November 16.
 At the event, honorees were recognized for standout performances and work, both on-screen and off-screen, from the Black entertainment community.
 Hosted by comedian Roy Wood Jr., the event will stream on the CCA’s official YouTube channel in December.
 RELATED: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’ Premiere Red Carpet Photos: Brad Pitt, Elizabeth Debicki, Quentin Tarantino & More 
 Honorees of the night included Debbie Allen (Icon Award), Abbott Elementary star and creator Quinta Brunson (Groundbreaker Award), Chiwetel Ejiofor (Vanguard Award), Chris Rock (Director Award), Lamorne Morris (Comedy Award) and Jaafar Jackson (Actor Award – Film).
 Other honorees include Anthony Mackie (Actor Award – Series), P-Valley’s Katori Hall (Showrunner Award), Stephan James (Supporting Actor Award – Film), Sophie Okonedo (Supporting Actress Award – Film), Ato Essandoh (Supporting Actor Award – Series) and Quincy Tyler Bernstine (Supporting Actress Award – Series).
 RELATED: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ NYC Premiere Red Carpet Photos: Jennifer Lawrence, Mckenna Grace, Rachel Zegler & More 
 Arie Esiri and Chuko Esiri will also receive the Breakthrough Director Award, while Jaalen Best will be honored with the Rising Star Award.
 The Critics Choice Association’s Celebration of Black Cinema & Television will be produced by Madelyn Hammond, Javier Infante, and Ella Carlson of Hammond Infante Productions.
